title: Choose Ratchet’s visual world
question: I’ve prepared one assigned direction, a grounded flight-recorder alternative, two full challenger directions, and the category-standard exit. Choose a direction or re-roll.

options.label: Ratchet Calibration Bench
options.thesis: A release moves across one friendly inspection bench, with each finding measured against the frozen declaration.
options.viewport: Studio Next status and the selected release sit above paired implementation hashes; Declared, Observed, and Decision align on a single inspection track.
options.risk: The workshop can become decoration unless every marker explains an evidence state.

raised.raise: Evidence gaps use sharply bounded, labeled slots so missing inputs are visible before a verdict.
Severity color stays in one restrained status rail; every state also gets a shape and label, with no flashing.
Release, attempt, and transaction IDs remain short, stable, and keyboard-addressable.
Status characters use a small discrete shape set and remain understandable with motion disabled.

options.label: The Release Flight Recorder
options.thesis: One continuous strip records what was declared, replayed, decided, and authorized.
options.viewport: The candidate ID and implementation hashes anchor a horizontal release trace, with the declared-to-observed difference visible before the verdict gate.
options.risk: Flight-recorder rails are familiar in this category; the evidence must give the device its own identity.

options.label: The Reversible Fold
options.thesis: Open each release stage as a reversible evidence fold; earlier steps stay recorded and recoverable.
materials: one warm marker per active step
options.viewport: The declaration begins as a folded cover; each deliberate reveal opens the matching replay observations and keeps prior evidence in view.
options.risk: Paper craft may feel too playful for a release decision, so rollback remains calm and explicit.
options.case: Competitive: the reversible reveal makes the evidence path easy to follow, but the paper-folding world identifies less strongly with release operators than a calibration bench.

options.label: The Registration Folio
options.thesis: Declared and observed changes share one scale and one ground, so drift is easy to spot.
options.viewport: A paired baseline and candidate plate share the same landmarks; declaration markers and replay differences register on those exact points.
options.risk: A folio can feel editorial; keep the typography engineered and the release action immediate.
options.case: Competitive: fixed-scale overlays strengthen product clarity, while a specimen folio is a weaker audience cue than an operations bench.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Evidence appears as weather blocks cut from a changing cloud wall.
options.viewport: A layered cloud field opens on the replay's missing and observed regions.
options.risk: The metaphor makes storage and permission evidence feel abstract.
options.case: Declined: it loses on audience identification and product clarity because the surreal quarry has no release-review convention.
options.kept: Missing evidence should occupy a sharply bounded, labeled space.

options.label: Crisis Wall
options.thesis: A release state fills a monumental alarm panel.
options.viewport: A giant state counter dominates a wall of release signals and condition bars.
options.risk: Alarm styling makes evidence review feel like an emergency.
options.case: Declined: the crisis-room language conflicts with the friendly brief and pushes the data into a generic command wall.
options.kept: Reserve strong severity color for a labeled state and never animate it as an alarm.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Release records are fixed-grid pages reached by a short address.
options.viewport: A numbered index page lists releases and their latest attempt.
options.risk: A strict retro grid reads as a fake terminal and constrains evidence legibility.
options.case: Declined: stable page addresses help, but the broadcast interface does not identify with release operators and obscures rich comparison.
options.kept: Give every release and evidence attempt a short, stable, keyboard-accessible reference.

options.label: Pixel Arcade
options.thesis: Upgrade differences appear as a tiled playfield.
options.viewport: The candidate and baseline form a grid of illuminated state tiles.
options.risk: The arcade frame gamifies a serious release outcome.
options.case: Declined: the game surface makes a rollback feel playful and does not improve operator understanding.
options.kept: Use a small, consistent set of discrete status shapes that still works without animation.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A straightforward operations dashboard with a two-column declaration and replay table.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional release overview above a comparison table.
canonCard.risk: The layout is familiar but less distinctive; it still needs excellent evidence hierarchy.
